Two New Factories. ₹2,010 Crore Order Book. One Company Building the Grid Behind India’s Energy Transition ⚡

The energy transition needs more than solar panels and batteries.

It also needs the specialised electrical equipment that keeps power flowing, stabilises grids and connects renewable generation to consumers.

Quality Power Electrical Equipment Private Limited is expanding into exactly this layer of the energy infrastructure.

The company’s latest update highlights several developments:

🔹 ₹2,010 crore order book: The consolidated order book has crossed ₹2,000 crore, spanning reactors, instrument transformers, power-conversion systems and FACTS solutions.

🔹 Sangli expansion: Its new Global Coil Factory began manufacturing operations on 20 October 2026, producing high-voltage air-core dry-type reactors and specialised coil products.

🔹 International manufacturing: Its Power Conversion Systems facility in Türkiye started operations on 16 October, focused on converters and inverters for utility-scale battery energy storage systems.

🔹 Strong H1 FY27: Revenue reached ₹550 crore, up 33.2% year-on-year, while EBITDA increased 52.2% and PAT rose 52.4% to ₹110 crore.

The company is also pursuing the acquisition of Winwin Speciality Insulators, which could broaden its high-voltage transmission product portfolio.

But the challenge is execution. Specialised electrical equipment faces raw-material, procurement, logistics and qualification pressures, while new facilities must reach efficient utilisation.

Could companies like Quality Power become critical beneficiaries of India’s next wave of grid modernisation, renewable integration and energy storage?

#QualityPower #PowerInfrastructure #EnergyTransition #HVDC #GridModernisation #RenewableEnergy #BatteryStorage #ElectricalEngineering #PowerEquipment #Manufacturing #CleanEnergy #IndianManufacturing #Infrastructure #EnergySector #AdvocateDavidChaudhary
comment: The real test will be how quickly these facilities move from commissioning to consistent utilisation. In grid equipment, qualification cycles and on-time delivery often matter as much as order book growth.
